key_insight: Entropy estimation in multi-qutrit systems transitions from variational quantum methods for small cases to CNN-based estimators that scale better and remain robust for larger systems.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a practical design rule for quantum sensing/estimation pipelines: use parameter-rich VQAs for up to three qutrits, then switch to measurement-driven classical models for higher-dimensional systems.
method: Evaluated 11 SU(3)-inspired hardware-efficient VQAs for up to three qutrits.
Trained a CNN on tensor-product mutually unbiased basis measurement outcomes for two to five qutrits.
Tested robustness under shot noise and out-of-distribution states in an ideal simulator setting.
evidence_signal: Across the simulated benchmarks, accuracy depended mainly on trainable parameter count when entanglement was sufficient, and the CNN achieved 90th-percentile absolute errors of about 0.13–0.16 nats for four- and five-qutrit systems using only 12.5% of full-tomography measurements.
watch_item: Results are based on noise-free simulation, so hardware execution may require retraining, calibration, and noise-mitigation to preserve performance.
paper_title: Entropy Estimation in Multi-Qutrit Systems via Variational and Classical Neural Networks
